question.text: The conflict spread when Germany attacked this neutral country hoping to capture Liege ("leezh") and outflank the French. Instead, Britain entered the war on the Allied side.
question.clue: One-third of the votes cast in an election in this country set up by the provisional government of Charles Rogier were left blank in protest.

swap.text: This company, based in Amsterdam, was given a monopoly on Dutch spice trade in 1602 and was one of the first major international corporations.
swap.answerHtml: Dutch East India Company [accept United East Indian Company]
swap.clue: It exported pepper from the Malukus, but was unable to displace Portuguese sandalwood traders from Timor.

question.leadin: William the Silent first led this country to its independance.
question.text: Name this country which fought the Eighty Years War for independence from Spain. Provinces in this country include North Holland and Zeeland (ZAY-lont).
question.clue: Batavia was a colonial city founded by this country, which drained lakes on its mainland to create polders.

swap.text: The longest river in South Africa has this name. A county by this name directly south of Los Angeles includes the cities of Anaheim, Huntington Beach, and Fullerton, in addition to being the site of Disneyland.
swap.clue: Safety regulations require the use of white alternating with this color in certain tower structures, such as the Yerevan TV Tower and the Tokyo Tower.

question.leadin: Commoners from this region collected 500 pairs of spurs from defeated French nobles during the Battle of the Golden Spurs.
question.text: Name this part of Northern Europe where the early modern wool trade flourished. Philip IV (the fourth) of France attempted to cement control of this region in a war from 1297 to 1305.
question.answerHtml: Flanders [or Flandre; or Vlaanderen; prompt on Belgium; prompt on Belge; prompt on the Low Countries]
question.clue: A shibboleth was used here prior to the Battle of the Golden Spurs, and parts of the "race to the sea" occurred here, ending after the opening of the sea-locks during the Battle of the Yser.

swap.leadin: Sea Beggars were used by one side during this conflict.
swap.text: Name this conflict which saw William the Silent and Maurice of Nassau fight the Duke of Alba for control of a certain country.
swap.clue: The first assassination of a head of state by handgun was carried out by Balthasar Gerard during this war.

question.leadin: In September of 1944, over 40,000 allied paratroopers were dropped near Arnhem in the Netherlands in an ambitious plan to end World War 2 by Christmas.
question.text: Name this failed operation. Its success depended on the taking and holding of several bridges.
question.clue: It was the last attempt to win the war by Christmas and had a strategic objective of forcing a crossing of the at .

swap.text: The Spanish feared the use of "hell-burners" which were used in the 1585 siege of this Flemish city. Today it is Europe's second busiest port city following Rotterdam.
swap.clue: Echoing Rome, the people of this city affixed the letters SPQA to its pioneering Beurs building.

question.leadin: This man became one of the first heads of state to die by handgun when Balthasar Gerard assassinated him in 1584.
question.text: Name this stadtholder who gave a speech on religious toleration in the Spanish Council of State and urged the Sea Beggars to petition Margaret of Parma to end religious persecution.
question.answerHtml: William the Silent [or William I, Prince of Orange, Count of Nassau or Willem I or Willem de Zwijger; prompt on "William of Orange"]
question.clue: This leader's main antagonist dubbed this person a "pest on the whole of Christianity" and offered a massive bounty on this person's head, which led to the first assassination of a head of state with a firearm.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about the violent history of Europe.
swap.text: Organized by the Duke of Alba, this court in the Spanish Netherlands attempted to suppress Calvinism and tighten Spanish control over the Netherlands by enforcing the Tenth Penny tax.
swap.answerHtml: Council of Blood [or Council of Troubles; or Raad Van Beroerten; or Bloedraad; or Tribunal de los Revoltosos; or Tribunal de Sangre; accept reasonable equivalents for "Council", such as "Court" ]
swap.clue: This tribunal created by the Duke of Alba to deal with unrest in the early stages of the Dutch Revolt.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about particularly old economic bubbles.
question.text: Tulip mania occurred in this nation in the 1630's when the speculation of Amsterdam-based traders drove the price of specific tulip bulbs incredibly high, only for the prices to suddenly crash.
question.answerHtml: Dutch Republic [or Republic of the Seven United Netherlands; prompt on “Holland”]
question.clue: The secret Treaty of Dover caused England to start a war with this polity during the "disaster year" of 1672.

swap.text: The Eighty Years War was sparked by a rebellion led by William the Silent, a member of this Dutch royal house.
swap.clue: A group supported by this dynasty that adopted crescent-shaped symbols for Ottoman support was the Sea Beggars.

question.leadin: Identify the following about important figures in the history of geography.
question.text: This Belgian-born cartographer is known today for his namesake style of projection, which distorts the poles.
question.clue: This University of Leuven scholar, who created a 1569 world map, led the "golden age of Netherlandish cartography." This engraver, who coined the term "atlas," names a widely-used but controversial map "projection."

swap.text: Many Flemish nationalists point to this battle during Philip IV's invasion of Flanders as a point of pride. Robert D'Artois ("dar-TWAH") was killed in this 1302 battle, named for a piece of equipment that was found littered on the battlefield after.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of the Golden Spurs [or Battle of Courtrai]
swap.clue: Stories of folk heroes who fought in this battle, such as the Cistercian lay brother Willem van Saeftinghe ("VILL-uhm vahn SAHF-ting-uh") and the weaver Pieter de Coninck, are romanticized in a novel by Hendrik Conscience ("kon-s'YAWNSS").

question.text: Though now only the eighth-largest city in the Netherlands, this city's historical importance is seen in its three changes of ownership during the Dutch war of independence and in Charles II's "declaration" from this city regarding the resumption of the English monarchy.
question.clue: A declaration named for this city was issued in response to an offer from General George Monck and promised to pardon all who recognized Charles II as the British monarch.

swap.leadin: In 1897, this woman moved to Java, where her brief marriage to the abusive army captain Rudolph MacLeod ended shortly after the death of their young son Norman, possibly poisoned by a housekeeper.
swap.text: Name this woman, known as "H-21" in official relays, but better known by a name meaning "eye of the day." Her services were recruited by Georges Ladoux, who would later tamper with evidence presented during her trial.
swap.answerHtml: Mata Hari [accept Margaretha Geertruida Zelle; prompt on Margaretha Geertruida MacLeod]
swap.clue: This person adopted a Malay name that meant "eye of the day" as a stage name.

question.text: In 1661, Portugal signed this treaty with the Dutch government of Johan de Witt. In it, Portugal ceded its possessions in Asia to the Dutch, but kept control of possessions in the New World and Africa.

swap.leadin: This city's first prince-bishop was the illustrious Notger, who had the Saint Lambert cathedral built.
swap.text: Name this so-called "Athens of the North," if by "North" you mean "Belgium," whose greatest Renaissance ruler was Erard de la Marck.
swap.clue: The strike of 1902, the second in a series of general strikes in Belgium, began when wildcat strikes broke out among miners in this province. This province faced a 1789 revolution called the Happy Revolution that restored the policies of Prince-Bishop Velbruck.

question.leadin: A sack of this city, which led Romain Rolland to call the Germans "descendants of Attila the Hun," was preceded by a similar action undertaken by Max von Hausen's army in Dinant.
question.text: A chapter of The Guns of August details the burning of a university library in what city by invading German forces?

swap.leadin: This action was caused when unpaid mercenaries decided to loot the central city and it stiffened Dutch resistance, hastening the signing of the Pacification of Ghent.
swap.text: Name this 1576 massacre often referred to as the Spanish Fury.
swap.clue: Otto Oberstein, drowned in the Scheldt while retreating from it, and the five thousand troops under the Marquis de Havre mostly failed to offer any resistance.
